clauses.scope_note: Section III expressly permits hosting the Model or a Derivative for third-party remote access, including as a software-as-a-service; the hosting permission is subject to the stated redistribution conditions.
clauses.condition_explanation: Section III, Distribution and Redistribution, lines 40–41: hosting for third-party remote access is permitted; applicable distribution conditions include the paragraph 5 provisions and notice where the Model or Derivative is governed by the agreement or distributed, and the recipient-license and notice-retention duties when copies are distributed. The paragraph 5 agreement and notification provision does not apply to use of Complementary Material.

clauses.scope_note: Patent grant includes selling the Model and Complementary Material, only within the qualifying patent-claim scope and subject to termination on specified patent litigation. This clause represents the expressly stated sale act; the grant also includes other acts not fully represented by the allowed activities.
clauses.condition_explanation: A qualifying patent claim must be licensable by the relevant Contributor and necessarily infringed by its Contribution alone or in combination with the Model to which the Contribution was submitted. The patent license terminates as of the date the licensee asserts or files patent litigation against any entity alleging direct or contributory infringement by the Model, Complementary Material, or an incorporated Contribution.

clauses.scope_note: Section III expressly says use may include creating content with, fine-tuning, updating, running, evaluating, or reparameterizing the Model. This supplements the general use restriction; it does not expand the permission beyond the License.
clauses.condition_explanation: The listed operations are examples of Use in Section III, Use-based restrictions (line 41). Attachment A (lines 55–67) supplies restricted purposes. Subject to the License, use must be lawful and not for an Attachment A restricted purpose.

clauses.scope_note: Section III expressly includes training the Model among possible uses, subject to the License and Attachment A restrictions.
clauses.condition_explanation: Section III, Use-based restrictions (line 41), lists training as a possible use. Attachment A (lines 55–67) restricts specified purposes; this is not an unrestricted training grant.

coverage_notes: Paragraph 4.a is referenced at line 40 but its text is not supplied; the additional-or-different-terms permission is preserved in the immutable anchor with that dependency, and no contents are inferred.

Lines 37–38 also grant acts such as public display, public performance, making, having made, offering to sell, and importing that do not have a faithful matching activity in the fixed vocabulary. Line 44 reserves Licensor powers to restrict usage, update the Model, or modify Output; those are Licensor actions, not licensee activities. These unmatched matters are identified in the paragraph audit rather than represented as fictitious permissions.
Line 46–47 warranty and liability disclaimers do not impose an activity duty. Line 49 severability is a legal effect that does not fit the fixed activity/object schema.

paragraph_audit.reason: The express permissions, conditions, and duties in lines 37–45 and 48 are represented by these clauses and the immutable anchors. Some separately stated acts (including public display/performance, making/having made, offering to sell, and importing) and Licensor’s reserved powers to restrict, update, or modify are not expressible as licensee activities in the fixed vocabulary. Lines 46–47 are warranty/liability disclaimers, not activity duties; line 49 is severability, outside activity scope. Paragraph 4.a remains an unavailable cross-reference.

Line 49 is a severability rule governing the legal effect of a provision being held invalid, illegal, or unenforceable; that legal effect cannot be faithfully represented as an activity constraint. Line 50 is an end-of-terms marker.
Line 55 introduces the Attachment A use restrictions. The immutable prohibition anchor covers the commitment, and its referenced restrictions are available in the full original at lines 57–67.
